title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Followup
summary: Follow-up on last week's POC reliability incidents (timeouts and 5xxs) during peak loads. Reviewed incident timeline, preliminary RCA from Redwood SE, short-term mitigations (retry/backoff, rate-limit bump, circuit breaker tuning), and longer-term actions (traces, guardrails, benchmark runs). Agreed next steps and owners.
next_steps: Alex Rivera: share aggregated error logs and sample X-Request-ID list by 2026-03-11
Priya Nair: propose retry/backoff config and circuit-breaker thresholds by 2026-03-12
David Lopez: run provided load-test script against staging and share results by 2026-03-13
Maya Singh: open ticket for temporary POC rate-limit increase and track ETA
Schedule deep-dive with Blueleaf infra team for 2026-03-15 (Alex to send invite)
action_items: Alex Rivera: collate and send error logs + X-Request-IDs (due 2026-03-11)
Priya Nair: draft tuning doc for retries/backoff and circuit breaker (due 2026-03-12)
David Lopez: run load test and attach spikes/latency CSVs (due 2026-03-13)
Anika Rao: confirm SOC2-encrypted log transfer method (due 2026-03-12)
Jordan Kim: follow up on temporary rate-limit increase request with ops (due 2026-03-11)
transcript: [00:00] Alex Rivera: ok thanks everyone for making time, this is the weekly POC sync. We flagged some reliability issues last week — timeouts and 5xx spikes during the afternoon run. we'll go through timeline and actions

[00:20] Michael Chen: yep thanks Alex, just to be clear the biggest impact was between 14:10 and 14:30 local, some user jobs failed with 504s and a few 500s, and our retry logic hit the rate limits quickly

[00:35] Priya Nair: quick note, we've pulled partial traces — looks like a mix of tokenization timeouts for long contexts and upstream 5xx from one of our inference nodes under CPU thrash. still piecing it together
[01:05] Sara Patel: we saw a pattern where the requests with long context windows and embeddings in the same flow had higher latency; might be KV cache misses? not sure
[01:30] David Lopez: to add, our orchestrator showed backpressure — the circuit breaker tripped on one pool, and then clients retried which amplified the problem, classic retry storm
[02:10] Alex Rivera: yeah that's what we want to avoid. Priya, does the preliminary RCA call it a retry amplification because of conservative backoff configs?

[02:25] Priya Nair: partly, yes. We saw exponential backoffs but small jitter and short max backoff — clients retried in similar windows. Also some requests hit a node with high GPU memory pressure causing 5xx, so not a pure network issue
[03:00] Anika Rao: on the security side, we need SAML-friendly logs and redaction. can the logs you share have PII redacted? we can't pull raw transcripts into our systems
[03:20] Alex Rivera: absolutely, we'll provide redacted logs and X-Request-ID lists so you can map traces without raw content
[03:40] Jordan Kim: i'll open a support ticket for a temporary rate-limit bump for the POC—this should reduce immediate client-side throttling while we tune retries
[04:05] Michael Chen: that would help. timeline wise, we're trying to validate daily ingest jobs — if we keep hitting throttles it's blocking our feature tests

[05:00] Priya Nair: one immediate suggestion: increase server-side circuit-breaker thresholds for the POC pool, add randomized jitter to retries client-side, and enable an aggressive KV cache warmup for repeated prefixes
[05:30] Sara Patel: can you be specific on numbers? what's "increase" mean?
[05:45] Priya Nair: good q. for POC, we can recommend a temporary 1.5x rate-limit increase and raise error-rate thresholds from 5% to 10% for the pool, while we observe. detailed doc incoming
[06:20] David Lopez: 1.5x ok as temporary, but we need an ops window. also want to see the traces that show which nodes returned 500s
[06:45] Alex Rivera: we'll include node IDs and X-Request-IDs. Priya, can you also include suggested backoff config (base, max, jitter)?
[07:05] Priya Nair: sure — base 200ms, max 4s, full jitter suggested. also, implement client-side cap on retries to 3 attempts and a cooldown when circuit breaker opens
[07:40] Michael Chen: that aligns with our policy. does Redwood support automatic client-side caps? our SDKs are configurable but we need specific values
[08:10] Priya Nair: yes our SDK supports configs; we'll send a snippet. note that some older internal clients might not pick up jitter by default
[08:40] Sara Patel: about the 5xx — is that hardware memory pressure or a model OOM? the logs said OOM in one place

[09:05] Priya Nair: preliminary looks like GPU memory pressure on a single node that was handling long sequences. model config had slightly higher kv-cache allocation after quantization testing. not a full OOM but transient failures leading to 5xx
[09:35] David Lopez: are you running different quantization variants for the POC? that might explain node-specific behavior
[09:55] Priya Nair: yes, the staging pool used a q4_0 variant for cost testing; we'll double-check kernel selection logs. we might pin the model variant till stability is proven
[10:20] Alex Rivera: pinned model variant + increased memory margin—good short term. long term we should revisit quantization profiles per workload
[10:45] Michael Chen: can we get the kernel selection trace? our team wants to see which kernels were chosen during the spike
[11:10] Priya Nair: will include those traces, with node IDs and timestamps. also include per-request latency percentiles so you can correlate

[11:40] Jordan Kim: linking to the benchmarking worksheet — we'll add a column for these incident runs so you can see before/after changes, link: https://docs.internal/blueleaf-poc/benchmarks (private)
[12:05] Sara Patel: perfect. one more Q — we saw some 429s earlier in the morning, separate from the 500s. are 429s related to tenant throttles or some upstream gateway?
[12:30] Priya Nair: 429s were tenant-side rate limiting; likely the orchestrator's per-tenant caps. the 5xx/timeouts were node-level degradation. both combined made the retry storm worse
[13:00] David Lopez: ok so root causes: tenant throttling + node memory pressure + retry amplification. action is multi-pronged
[13:25] Alex Rivera: exactly. immediate mitigations listed: temporary rate-limit bump (ops), pin model variant, backoff+jitter + cap retries, and increase circuit-breaker thresholds for the POC pool
[13:55] Anika Rao: for security/compliance: we need to record the audit events and have KMS encryption on logs transferred. is Redwood OK with S3 server-side encryption + KMS?
[14:20] Maya Singh: yes we support S3 SSE+KMS for log exports and can do an encrypted pre-signed transfer; we'll document the workflow
[14:45] Michael Chen: good. about the request IDs — can you send a sample CSV so our infra can crosswalk with our logs?
[15:05] Alex Rivera: yes, next step. i'll send a redacted CSV of request IDs and node timestamps
[15:30] Priya Nair: operational note — we recommend temporarily moving heavy batch jobs to off-peak windows while we stabilize. did you run the parallel ingest at 14:00?
[15:50] Sara Patel: yes that was the bulk job. we'll shift tomorrow and rerun tests
[16:20] David Lopez: we'll run the load script you shared last week with the peak profile and collect p99s, and attach the CSVs
[16:45] Alex Rivera: great. Jordan will track the rate-limit increase ticket. Priya will draft the retry/circuit-breaker doc and include SDK snippets
[17:10] Michael Chen: can we also get a quick live demo of toggling the pool config? we may want to see how fast changes propagate
[17:35] Priya Nair: yes quick demo next call or we can do an ad-hoc session. changes usually take a few minutes to roll across the pool during POC config pushes
[18:00] Sara Patel: just a heads-up some internal clients have older SDK versions; we might need Redwood to provide a patch or code snippet for them
[18:25] Priya Nair: we'll include a compatibility note in the doc and snippet for v1.2 and v1.3 SDKs

[19:00] Alex Rivera: ok let's recap — we'll send logs, request IDs, kernel traces; propose retry/backoff and circuit-breaker params; Jordan to request temp rate-limit increase; Blueleaf to run load tests and shift batch to off-peak. meet again next Tue unless we need an earlier deep-dive
[19:30] Michael Chen: sounds good, thanks everyone. any open blockers?
[19:45] Anika Rao: none on security as long as logs are redacted and encrypted
[20:00] Jordan Kim: ticket created: RF-1420 temporary rate-limit request (tracking link will be shared)
[20:20] Alex Rivera: perfect. i'll send meeting notes and a prioritized action list after this. thanks all
[20:35] Meeting end
